x: Pirie, Norris and Foord fought it out all the way and our chaps were never in the hunt for the leading positions. Our leading runner just managed to beat South London's 6th, but by some remarkable packing, six men in 14 places and 64 seconds, we gained second place in the team race.

The eighth leg was run by Bedford who was only too pleased to run whereever the selectors decided and though he lost places to Norris and Clark he still gave a sterling performance and established a new club best by 10 seconds.

… generally was of a high standard and some excellent competition was seen, especially in the three miles with Sando and Norris running the whole distance together and finishing only inches apart in the wonderful time of 13 mins. 29.8 secs. which at that time was only 3.4secs outside the world record…
Similarly T.V.H. who were 13th at Purley, were up to third at Merstham only five miles further on, by the amazing performance of Ken Norris.
Archie Bedford ran well over the 4th stage but quite naturally was unable to cope with record runs by Norris and Sando and was relegated to 8th place.

On the 9th stage, Dave Maclean found this flat course well to his liking and produced a fast time, though without altering our position. With Norris on the last stage for T.V.H. Chas Walker ambled round and we finished 2nd to Thames Valley with Herne Hill 3rd.
Thames Valley, however, were represented by Norris and added 10 more seconds to their lead. Jim produced the second best time and closed up the gap on the intervening clubs - an excellent effort.
Yet again the Arthur Whitehead "dustbin" sent the field on its way and after a ½ mile Pat Newell was 14th with Chanin(S.L.H.) leading from Ibbottson and Norris.
The 15 miles was covered in 78:29.4, and although Fred Norris's English Native Record was set en route to a longer distance, Charlie was only 65 secs. outside the official mark.
Then, even allowing the criminal handicap of altitude running, can we in any way equate Messrs Herriot, Taylor and Blinston with the Ibbotsons, Piries and Norrises of little more than a decade ago.
